title: Ringed local open-closed short exact sequence
statement: Let i:Z to X be a closed immersion with complementary quasi-compact open object U [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let A be any commutative ring sheaf. For actual module inverse image and direct image through the ring-unit action [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and the specified sheafified extension presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], let ai and aj be any adjunctions to their indicated right adjoints. At every A-module sheaf M, aj.counit(M) is monic, ai.unit(M) is epic, and the composable pair is exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence].

proof.text: Form the counit $\epsilon:j_!j^{-1}M\to M$ and unit $\eta:M\to i_*i^{-1}M$. The affine covering-family node first gives a cover by affine objects $T=\operatorname{Spec}C$ in the fixed small site. For each such $C$, choose an infinite $\mathcal U$-small cardinal $\kappa\geq |C|$ and apply the bounded ring-extension node. It supplies a one-member pro-etale covering $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\to T$ with $|R|\leq\kappa^{2^{2^{2^\kappa}}}$ and, crucially, retractions of every faithfully flat weakly etale map out of $R$. The bound is still $\mathcal U$-small: a Grothendieck universe is closed under power sets and function sets. Prime ideals, localizations, and the structure sheaf of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ are built from subsets, quotients of pairs, and function sets of $R$, so the resulting affine scheme is $\mathcal U$-bounded; choose its representative in the site's skeleton. Ind-etale maps are weakly etale, and weakly etale maps compose, by the stability node. Thus $V\to X$ is an object of the same small site. These refinements cover every original object by the transitivity axiom of a site. We now use the ring splitting property furnished by the ring-extension statement itself, rather than infer it for unrestricted algebras from small-site weak contractibility. Write $V_Z=V\times_X Z=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$. Clause (3) of the qcqs-morphism permanence node makes the base change $V\times_X U\to V$ of the quasi-compact $j$ quasi-compact. Since $V$ is affine, its inverse image of the affine open $V$ is the whole $V\times_X U=V\setminus V_Z$, which is consequently a quasi-compact open, and $V\setminus V_Z=\bigcup_{f\in I}D(f)$ by the definition of $V(I)$. Basic opens are open; compactness selects finitely many $f_k\in I$ covering this complement, so $V(I)=V(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. The closed-localization node gives a covering of $V$ by $V_k=\operatorname{Spec}R_{f_k}$ and $V^\sim=\operatorname{Spec}S^{-1}R$, where $S$ consists of elements invertible modulo $I$. On each $V_k$, step 1 identifies $\epsilon$ with the identity and the target of $\eta$ with zero. Every point of $V^\sim$ specializes into its closed fibre, and $S^{-1}R$ is w-contractible; Both $S^{-1}R$ and $R_{f_k}$ are quotients of subsets of $R\times R$, hence remain $\mathcal U$-small; their spectra are bounded by the same subset/function-set argument. The closed-localization covering statement makes their maps to $V$ weakly etale, so the stability node makes the composites to $X$ objects of the same site. Applying the ring-to-site weak-contractibility node to the actual w-contractible ring $S^{-1}R$ and this verified site object shows that $V^\sim$ is weakly contractible on the full small site. The shriek-specialization-zero node makes the source of $\epsilon$ zero there, and the specialization-restriction-sections node identifies $\eta(V^\sim)$ with the identity. These are the actual unit and counit maps, not just abstract identifications of their objects. On this covering family the sequence is therefore either $0\to M\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}M\to0\to0$ or $0\to0\to M\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}M\to0$. The composite vanishes locally and hence globally; kernels and images agree locally and therefore globally, and local lifting of sections proves the last map epic. Forgetting module actions computes these exactness conditions; the maps are linear because the presheaf counit and inverse-image unit commute with multiplication. This proves the claimed short exact sequence without using geometric stalk conservativity. Changing ai or aj changes the end maps by isomorphisms of source or target; all three asserted conditions are preserved.

theorem proEtale_ringed_localization_sequence {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (U : X.ProEt) [IsOpenImmersion U.hom] [QuasiCompact U.hom]
    (hU : Set.range U.hom = (Set.range i)ᶜ)
    (A : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (ai : proEtaleModuleInverseImage i A ⊣
      (SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u + 1} (F := proEtaleBaseChange i)
      (J := ProEt.topology X) (K := ProEt.topology Z)
      (S := ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology X)
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj A)) (R := ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology Z)
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj
        ((proEtaleSheafInverseImage i CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj A)))
      ⟨Functor.whiskerRight
        ((proEtaleSheafAdjunction i CommRingCat.{u + 1}).unit.app A).hom
        (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})⟩))
    (aj : (SheafOfModules.extensionByZeroPresheaf.{u + 1} ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology X)
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj A) U ⋙
      PresheafOfModules.sheafification (𝟙 ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology X)
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj A).obj)) ⊣
      SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u + 1} ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology X)
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj A) U) :
    ∀ M, Mono (aj.counit.app M) ∧ Epi (ai.unit.app M) ∧
      (ComposableArrows.mk₂ (aj.counit.app M) (ai.unit.app M)).Exact
